a.text: Where did you leave off...? Ah yes, on the eve of Samhain, while the sun still hung in the sky.
Samhain nights bind life with death. This is no mere superstition. Or perhaps you could say it has long transcended superstition.
Taran legends speak of countless great deeds and tragedies occurring on this very night, and such tales often put the date front and center.

So long as innumerable legends coincide on that day, and so long as the Tarans still remember, if only vaguely, to celebrate the harvest and light up fires on that day, it will never be a simple change of season.
It itself is the perfect footnote to add to any myth.
...Oh, and another thing. I don't suppose you'd mind if I gave the characters more fitting names, yes?
Have we yet to figure out how to go about this final confrontation?

steps.name: Cold Young Dragon
steps.text: Loughshinny, why are you hiding in your room at dinnertime again?

steps.name: Warm Young Dragon
steps.text: Is Dad angry?

steps.name: Cold Young Dragon
steps.text: No, but he will be soon.

steps.name: Warm Young Dragon
steps.text: I'll be down soon—

steps.name: Cold Young Dragon
steps.text: What's that on your desk?

steps.name: Warm Young Dragon
steps.text: Nothing!
The young red dragon tries to block her sister's line of sight with her body, but her effort is in vain.
A small paper box sits on her desk, carefully lined with cotton. Inside lies a tiny fowlbeast—already dead but still harboring a faint lingering warmth.
It seems to have broken its leg while alive. An unsuccessful splint fashioned from stiff paper now lies in pieces around it, accompanied by a few grains of wheat.

steps.name: Warm Young Dragon
steps.text: This is the fowlbeast that sang at my window every morning. I don't know what happened to it, but... I wanted to save it, and...

steps.name: Warm Young Dragon
steps.text: I beg of you, Sister—Tell Dad I'm only feeling ill. I'll be on time for dinner tomorrow... I'll bury it in the courtyard tonight.

steps.name: Cold Young Dragon
steps.text: So you're giving up?

steps.name: Warm Young Dragon
steps.text: It's already dead.

steps.name: Cold Young Dragon
steps.text: Is that so?
Purple flames slip past the fowlbeast's feathers into its already cold body.
The two watch as it slowly stands up, its broken leg stiffly propping itself up on the cotton.

steps.name: Cold Young Dragon
steps.text: Alright. Would you like it to fly, or to sing a song for you?

steps.name: Warm Young Dragon
steps.text: N-No! This isn't right! Not like this!

steps.name: Cold Young Dragon
steps.text: Then why didn't you use your own flames on it while it was still alive?

steps.name: Cold Young Dragon
steps.text: Your fowlbeast could have lived a much longer life. You do realize you aren't limited to how the mediocre masses do things, don't you?

steps.name: Warm Young Dragon
steps.text: But Mum told me to swallow my flames, hide them away, and never let them be seen...

steps.name: Cold Young Dragon
steps.text: And who would see them in your own room?
The young dragon looks away to avoid her sister's eyes, but finds her gaze landing on the fowlbeast standing on its cotton bed instead.
Purple fire burns in its eyes, and even the way it tilts its head is the spitting image of her sister.

a.text: Or do we perhaps still harbor unrealistic fantasies for how this could end?

steps.name: Noble Red Dragon
steps.text: Sister, you're covered in blood... were you injured?!

steps.name: Greedy Red Dragon
steps.text: Most of it isn't mine. The Duke's spy bled profusely.

steps.name: Noble Red Dragon
steps.text: I'll replace your bandages.

steps.name: Greedy Red Dragon
steps.text: Where is the Earl of Warwick?

steps.name: Noble Red Dragon
steps.text: He has... work to do.

steps.name: Greedy Red Dragon
steps.text: Yes, so he says. And as always, you take him at his word.

steps.name: Greedy Red Dragon
steps.text: He even allowed the spy to discuss poetry with you while he 'works'.

steps.name: Noble Red Dragon
steps.text: I thought I'd been keeping mum about our origins, as well as anything related to the Earl's vision...

steps.name: Greedy Red Dragon
steps.text: Everyone in this manor knows you never say a word more than necessary. That has never been something the Earl would bother to check.

steps.name: Greedy Red Dragon
steps.text: That's right. Had we let the spy escape, the Earl would still inevitably find a way to silence him in the dark, and we'd simply find ourselves bound by yet another chain called caution.

steps.name: Noble Red Dragon
steps.text: I'm sorry, I—

steps.name: Greedy Red Dragon
steps.text: There's no need for you to apologize. Apologies have never changed a thing.
Once packed with guests, the long-empty parlor's acoustics now amplify the sound of the bandages being ripped apart, making the atmosphere even heavier.

steps.name: Greedy Red Dragon
steps.text: Those poems by that Seamus Williams you've been so into... If you can remember them, why not recite a line or two for me?
The noble red dragon racks her brains for a verse that would not rouse her sister's rage. Perhaps something related to Tara, brave warriors, or even ancient legends—
But all she can recall are verses that stand aloof from worldly affairs.

steps.name: Noble Red Dragon
steps.text: 'The land is but a strange romance, the cause of its end lost to chance ill.'

steps.name: Noble Red Dragon
steps.text: 'I am but a wandering bard, well-versed in lore from songs in the woods...'
She sneaks a peek at her sister's face and sees no change, so she plucks up her courage and continues to recite more lines.
Only when she finishes both the entire poem and the new bandage with a delicate knot does she realize that her sister has already fallen asleep, encircled by meter and rhyme.

steps.name: Noble Red Dragon
steps.text: Sister.

steps.name: Greedy Red Dragon
steps.text: Ah, Loughshinny. You've kept me waiting.

steps.name: Greedy Red Dragon
steps.text: What of your new friends? The wayward wakewoman, or perhaps that lively nomad?

steps.name: Greedy Red Dragon
steps.text: With your presence, any obstacles preventing you from bringing them along should have easily been reduced to naught.

steps.name: Noble Red Dragon
steps.text: They're in the city, but this is a moment to be shared by us alone.

steps.name: Greedy Red Dragon
steps.text: Indeed.

steps.name: Greedy Red Dragon
steps.text: It's cold out here on the balcony, so let us continue this in the corridor.

steps.name: Noble Red Dragon
steps.text: A replica of where Labhréathach died, in Na Saoirsí... Why must you cling onto our inglorious history and repeat it?

steps.name: Greedy Red Dragon
steps.text: I see you've gained a deeper understanding of the word Tara.

steps.name: Greedy Red Dragon
steps.text: But if history does not repeat itself, then how can we speak of breaking the cycle?

a.text: It can be very difficult to tell us apart by appearance.
But the moment either of us speaks, it becomes as clear as night and day.
Eblana only ever steers the conversation toward her own interests, while Loughshinny is ever the polite one.
She'd get to the bottom of this and find an ending—
Don't interrupt me, sir. I'm talking about the characters in the story.

steps.name: Noble Red Dragon
steps.text: I'm sorry, Eblana.

steps.name: Greedy Red Dragon
steps.text: No, I'm quite glad. You finally accepted my invitation.

steps.name: Noble Red Dragon
steps.text: To dance?

steps.name: Noble Red Dragon
steps.text: Yes. To dance.

steps.name: Noble Red Dragon
steps.text: I'll dance with you to the end, together. However...

steps.name: Noble Red Dragon
steps.text: Please tell me first. The last time we met, you said you couldn't afford to wait any longer... What exactly is going on?

With that same smile of hers, the older sister stands at the end of the corridor, while the younger clutches her hands together and hides in the shadow of a wall lamp, hoping the other party won't notice her heart wavering.
Poor thing. She could have concluded this farewell so much sooner.

steps.name: Noble Red Dragon
steps.text: You've become... frail.

steps.name: Noble Red Dragon
steps.text: The flames of death must have their limits. Spreading them so far would certainly drag you down as fire after fire blooms, just like Labhréathach back then... Am I right?

steps.name: Greedy Red Dragon
steps.text: I see. While that ghost's fire might resemble mine, his temperament is closer to yours. It seems he's helped you quite a lot.

steps.name: Greedy Red Dragon
steps.text: At first he only wanted to watch all of Tara burn.

steps.name: Noble Red Dragon
steps.text: He was simply trying to keep it together...

steps.name: Noble Red Dragon
steps.text: Just like you.
The noble red dragon finally steps out of the shadows, walking forward to support her sister who seems on the verge of being unable to stand... just like before.

steps.name: Greedy Red Dragon
steps.text: Is that so?

steps.name: Greedy Red Dragon
steps.text: At last you resemble your younger self, when you knew nothing of flames or fate. The you who tried to shield me.

steps.name: Greedy Red Dragon
steps.text: It has been a truly long time, Loughshinny.

steps.name: Noble Red Dragon
steps.text: I remember. It was when Mrs. Murphy next door passed away. You didn't like her, but fancied the beautiful bouquet of flowers in her coffin...

steps.name: Noble Red Dragon
steps.text: So you used your flames to change her body's position.

steps.name: Noble Red Dragon
steps.text: I saw scorch marks on the flowers and thought you'd be scolded, so I told our parents I was the one who did it. I even fabricated a story of how I opened and closed the coffin...

steps.name: Greedy Red Dragon
steps.text: And so you were scolded instead.

steps.name: Greedy Red Dragon
steps.text: How could poor Mum and Dad—who couldn't even hide the flames in that family in time—possibly have noticed the faint scorch marks on some flowers?

steps.name: Noble Red Dragon
steps.text: ...Indeed.

steps.name: Greedy Red Dragon
steps.text: Is that why you've always been cowering?

steps.name: Noble Red Dragon
steps.text: Would you blame every decision you've made in life on one unfortunate childhood experience?

spans.text: blame every decision you've made in life on one unfortunate childhood experience?

steps.name: Greedy Red Dragon
steps.text: ...Hah.

steps.name: Noble Red Dragon
steps.text: So tell me, Sister. Tell me there's still time.

steps.name: Noble Red Dragon
steps.text: I'll accompany you out of the citadel and into the square. Have the people return their flames to you.

steps.name: Noble Red Dragon
steps.text: I'll walk through Tara's fields with you, and gather the dead you've intentionally or unintentionally awoken with your Arts, sending them all to a peaceful rest.

steps.name: Noble Red Dragon
steps.text: I'll recite poems to you while you're weak, until you fall asleep and wake up again.

steps.name: Noble Red Dragon
steps.text: There's still time for all of that, yes?

steps.name: Greedy Red Dragon
steps.text: I trust you to keep your word. Your noble nature would be appalled at the very thought of breaking a promise.

steps.name: Greedy Red Dragon
steps.text: But what you just described, would that truly make you happy?

steps.name: Greedy Red Dragon
steps.text: Or would that simply be enough to appease the Loughshinny Dublinn who did not even witness her parents' death, that snowy night? Those... beautiful fictions?

steps.name: Greedy Red Dragon
steps.text: Sister. Love, poetry, dreams—those are all well and good, but it is time for you to wake up.

steps.name: Greedy Red Dragon
steps.text: Kill me. If you truly wish to end this chaos, that is the only way.

steps.name: Greedy Red Dragon
steps.text: Then, put on the crown, and you shall become me, while I become you.

steps.name: Noble Red Dragon
steps.text: That is the one thing I cannot do.

steps.name: Greedy Red Dragon
steps.text: You'll have time to mull over it once I'm dead.

steps.name: Greedy Red Dragon
steps.text: Didn't you decide not to hesitate anymore, Loughshinny?

steps.name: Greedy Red Dragon
steps.text: There's been no other choice for us from the moment you came back to see me.
The older sister's mouth curls up in an intriguing arc.

steps.name: Greedy Red Dragon
steps.text: Come, dance with me.

steps.name: Noble Red Dragon
steps.text: Is this... the dance you've been looking forward to all this time?

steps.name: Greedy Red Dragon
steps.text: Why can't it be?
The younger sister closes her eyes as she points her spear at her older sister, whose body is about to topple over. She grips her weapon with both hands.
The sharp speartip pierces the red dragon's body, but she stands unmoved, as if nothing happened at all, until her younger sister's hand circles her waist, and her body slowly crumples.
...Just like the end of a dance.

steps.name: Noble Red Dragon
steps.text: Yes, I know.

steps.name: Noble Red Dragon
steps.text: I should have known long ago.

steps.name: Noble Red Dragon
steps.text: But why? Why must it be now?

steps.name: Greedy Red Dragon
steps.text: ...Then when?

steps.name: Greedy Red Dragon
steps.text: Don't tell me you'd prefer to stab my heart on a fine afternoon, after meticulously dissecting every nuance of right and wrong with me?

steps.name: Greedy Red Dragon
steps.text: You returned to me, and we danced this dance together. That's enough.

steps.name: Noble Red Dragon
steps.text: I only thought... if my sorrow and hatred were thrown into a suitable flame, they'd eventually become the fuel for life to go on.

steps.name: Greedy Red Dragon
steps.text: Sorrow, and hatred... so you admit it, Loughshinny.

steps.name: Greedy Red Dragon
steps.text: Your noble virtues have only hurt you in the end. Where is your fire, Sister?

steps.name: Noble Red Dragon
steps.text: I can't put out your flames just like that.

steps.name: Greedy Red Dragon
steps.text: Hah, you mean... the people in the city?

steps.name: Noble Red Dragon
steps.text: You will die, but not now. Your flames will be extinguished at your funeral, at your fire-returning ceremony.

steps.name: Greedy Red Dragon
steps.text: But still, you ought to be dispelling death with scorching flames, rather than holding the hand of the dead and confessing your own inner turmoil, your own regrets. Otherwise...

steps.name: Greedy Red Dragon
steps.text: You will only ever be as you are now, letting go of your chance to save everything... your final chance.
The noble red dragon loosens her grip in shock, and her sister's body drops to the ground, as cold as it was before her heart was pierced.
It is not blood but purple fire that roars from the wound spanning her entire torso. It instantly floods the balcony and flows down the citadel.
The noble red dragon rushes over to the balcony, but the purple flames of death are even faster.
Before her own flames can emit even the tiniest spark of light, the purple fire spreads across the city, burning the whole of Na Saoirsí.
The last time she looked out from this very spot, the flames were scattered like stars in the sky. When she had returned earlier that day, they coated the whole city with a cold and gloomy hue.
And now...
Na Saoirsí itself burns fiercely, just like every other restless corpse she has seen.
